kurz: Mix starch with cold water, stir it into the simmering sauce and bring it briefly to the boil. Quick, reliable and without a floury taste.
bild_im_kopf: Like water beads spread out one by one beforehand: tipped into hot liquid, they clump together at once.
was_passiert: In cold water the [[staerke|starch]] granules disperse without [[quellen|swelling]]. In the hot sauce they swell everywhere at once and thicken it. Cornflour needs a moment of boiling for this; after that the sauce is glossy and thick.
faustregeln: Better a little twice than too much once.
Long boiling and vigorous stirring make starch-thickened sauces thin again.
schritte: Stir 1 tbsp cornflour smooth in 2–3 tbsp cold water.
Bring briefly to the boil once.
Check, and add a little more if needed.
